concerns.location: research.md: Dataset Strategy table; plan.md Phase 0/1
concerns.text: The two 'LLM' datasets (davanstrien/authors_merged_model_prs, authors_merged_dataset_prs) are collections of PRs authored by LLM agents on HuggingFace Hub repositories (model-card/dataset-metadata updates), while the 'Human' control (loubnabnl/prs-v2-sample) is a general GitHub PR sample. The LLM and Human groups are therefore drawn from different platforms and different PR populations (metadata edits vs. general code changes), confounding any review-burden comparison by dataset origin. The plan concatenates all three files as if they were one homogeneous population. Either justify population comparability or select a control group matched to the HF-Hub PR population.

The davanstrien authors_merged_* datasets are curated specifically because PRs were LLM-authored; they plausibly lack review-interaction fields (comment_count, first_comment_timestamp, review comments, labels) that HF Hub PR dumps often omit. The plan's Dataset-Variable Fit gate would then halt the pipeline AFTER download because outcome variables are missing in the entire LLM arm. A planning-stage check of the actual column sets (or a stated fallback dataset for the LLM group) is needed; deferring this entirely to runtime risks the whole design being unrunnable as written.

The fit gate treats first_comment_timestamp/diff_text/file_headers as merely 'at risk', but for the davanstrien datasets these fields are near-certainly absent (HF Hub PR metadata), meaning FR-002's precedence collapses to commit-message-only for the entire LLM group and FR-016's primary metric falls back for that group. The plan should state this expected degradation per-dataset rather than presenting it as a symmetric runtime contingency.
